title: Ar-Ra'uf, the Most Kind
hook: the Most Kind, tender in compassion
tomorrow: Eli says a wall belongs to whoever paints it. whose wall is it?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-'Afuww, the Pardoner, and the one-line prayer for the Night of Power. The line: erased. Pardon wipes the trace. Today's question is about the tone of voice that comes after.

Two lines go around online. One says: protect your peace, cut them off. The other says: be kind, everyone's carrying something. Yesterday's question lives right between them. Is tenderness toward someone who wronged you a strength, or a leak? Today's Name is Ar-Ra'uf, the Most Kind, tender in compassion. And scholars of the Names read this word in two different ways. Both deserve a hearing.
screen: `CUT THEM OFF, OR BE KIND?` → `STRENGTH, OR A LEAK?` → `TWO READINGS.`

segments.voice: Start with the verse. In Pickthall's words: "Lo! Allah is full of pity, Merciful toward mankind." Ra'uf and Rahim, side by side. So if Allah is already the Merciful, what does Ra'uf add? The first reading says: degree. Ra'fa is rahma turned all the way up, mercy at its most intense and most tender. Al-Ghazali, in his book on the Names, describes it this way. On this view, tenderness isn't a weak form of mercy. It's the strongest. The second reading says: direction. Other commentators hear ra'fa as the mercy that lifts a burden and keeps hardship away, while rahma can include a good that stings, like medicine. They point to a verse about the Prophet, peace be upon him: "unto whom aught that ye are overburdened is grievous, full of concern for you, for the believers full of pity, merciful." Your weight is heavy on him. On this view, tenderness is precise: it notices exactly what someone is carrying. And here's the detail to tell a friend tonight. In that verse, the Qur'an describes the Prophet with the same two words it uses for God, ra'uf and rahim. Neither reading makes tender mean silent. The one described as full of pity is the same one who delivered the hardest messages.
screen: `FULL OF PITY, MERCIFUL.` · `ONE READING: MERCY TURNED ALL THE WAY UP.` · `THE OTHER: MERCY THAT LIFTS A BURDEN.` · `THE SAME TWO WORDS, FOR THE PROPHET.` · then, large: `TENDER.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person carrying something heavy right now: a friend mid-exams, a parent who's tired, a neighbor who's alone. Write them a short, tender text, with no advice and no fixing, only that you noticed. Send it, or keep it ready, and let them stay in mind for the rest of the sit.
screen: `SOMEONE CARRYING SOMETHING.` · `NO ADVICE. JUST: I NOTICED.`

segments.voice: Ar-Ra'uf. The Most Kind: mercy at its most tender, the kind that feels the weight someone is carrying.
Your line: tender, which isn't the same thing as silent, and is never the same as weak. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Muslims call on Allah with paired Names, as the Qur'an pairs them: ya Ra'uf, ya Rahim, O Most Kind, O Most Merciful.

match.prompt: two readings of one Name — tap the pairs.

the Qur'an describes the Prophet with ra'uf and rahim, words it also uses for God
"for the believers full of pity, merciful."

fork.setup: you read ra'fa as mercy that lifts a burden. your friend reads it as mercy turned all the way up. what's the best case for your friend's side?
options: if mercy has degrees, tender is its strongest setting, so it can't be weak.
tender means you never say anything hard to anyone at all.
both readings say the same thing, so there's really nothing to argue.
fork.reveal: the first reading, given by al-Ghazali, makes tenderness the peak of mercy. the second sees mercy aimed at someone's weight. both are real readings; neither makes tender mean silent.

original.note: Arabic: the Most Kind, a Name of Allah; the Qur'an pairs it with Rahim, Merciful.

trapdoor: what you thought: a God who's nice.
what it means: tender compassion, either mercy at its height or mercy that lifts the weight off someone.
what a scholar hears: al-Ghazali reads ra'fa as intensified rahma; others as mercy that removes hardship; 2:143 and 9:128 both say ra'uf and rahim side by side.
guess: the Most Kind, tender in compassion
the Most Patient, slow to anger
the Most Gentle, never stern at all

chat.says: Eli's mom brought him by. he stared at his shoes. jordan says 'go easy.' i say lecture. who's right?
options: Maybe both. Tender means seeing what he's carrying, and still saying the wall matters.
Jordan. Tender means you never say anything hard to someone who's sorry.
You. Being tender after a wrong just teaches him he can do it again.
chat.meaning: Ar-Ra'uf is tender, and in 9:128 tenderness feels another's burden. That isn't the same as staying silent about what happened.
